Project Description: The Myntdu Leshka HEP Stage-II located in West and East Jaintia Hills District of Meghalaya State is planned as a Run-of-the-river for hydropower development of the river Myntdu. The project envisages utilization of the available head between El. 270 m (FRL) and El. 13 m (TWL). The river water is proposed to be diverted by building a 46 m high concrete gravity dam on Myntdu River wherein the diverted water is planned to be passed through a 6.175 km long headrace tunnel of 6.0 m dia. terminating in a surge shaft. A surface powerhouse housing 3 Francis Turbines of 70 MW each with an operating rated head of 239.17 m is proposed on the right bank of the river. Tailwater from the powerhouse will be discharged back into the Myntdu river. The project would annually generate about 593.04 MU energy in a 90% dependable year.

Project Description:
The NERPSIP scheme is a Govt. of India and World Bank funded project on a 50:50 basis. It is a project to address the poor power scenario in the region by capacity enhancement of interstate power transmission and infrastructure facilities by construction of new sub-stations, transmission lines and augmentation of old sub-stations. The project once completed will be handed over to the concern state utilities.
At present the people living in the areas like Tikrikilla, Raksamgre, Photamati, etc. where the project is being implemented are deprived of modern living facilities and conditions and cannot even start a small or medium level industries due to frequent power cut and very low voltage profile in the areas. After the completion of this new 33 KV line from Phulbari to Tikrikilla, the areas under 44-Raksamgre ST Constituencies and 45-Tikrikilla ST Constituencies will have better and more reliable power supply thereby solving the long plaguing issues of the region.

Project Description: The Myntdu Leshka HEP Stage-II located in West and East Jaintia Hills District of Meghalaya State is planned as a Run-of-the-river for hydropower development of the river Myntdu. The project envisages utilization of the available head between El. 270 m (FRL) and El. 13 m (TWL). The river water is proposed to be diverted by building a 46 m high concrete gravity dam on Myntdu River wherein the diverted water is planned to be passed through a 6.175 km long headrace tunnel of 6.0 m dia. terminating in a surge shaft. A surface powerhouse housing 3 Francis Turbines of 70 MW each with an operating rated head of 239.17 m is proposed on the right bank of the river. Tailwater from the powerhouse will be discharged back into the Myntdu river. The project would annually generate about 593.04 MU energy in a 90% dependable year.
